disclaimer: This explains your report in plain words. It is not a diagnosis and not medical advice. Only your doctor can tell you what these results mean for you.

note.what: This test measures glucose, the main sugar your body uses for energy, in blood taken after at least eight hours without food.
note.ask: What does my fasting blood sugar mean for me, and do I need another test to confirm it?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/blood-glucose-test/ (updated 30 December 2024)
note.means: A higher result can be a sign of prediabetes or diabetes, and is sometimes seen with thyroid, pancreas or adrenal problems, serious illness, or certain medicines.

note.what: HbA1c shows your average blood sugar over the past few months, because glucose sticks to haemoglobin inside your red blood cells.
note.ask: What HbA1c is healthy for me, and do I need a second test to confirm this result?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/hemoglobin-a1c-hba1c-test/ (updated 20 May 2025)
note.means: A higher result can be a sign of prediabetes or diabetes, and is usually confirmed with another test such as fasting glucose.

note.what: LDL is the 'bad' cholesterol, the chief contributor to the fatty build-up that can narrow or block your arteries.
note.ask: Was my LDL measured directly or calculated, and what does my level mean for my heart risk?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/cholesterol-levels/ (updated 15 October 2024)
note.means: A higher LDL raises the risk of coronary artery and other heart disease, which can lead to heart attack, stroke or blocked blood flow to the limbs.

note.what: Triglycerides are a type of fat your body uses for energy; this test measures how much of them is in your blood.
note.ask: Do I need to fast before this test, and what do my triglycerides mean for my heart risk?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/triglycerides-test/ (updated 9 December 2024)
note.means: A higher result can add to the risk of heart disease, stroke and metabolic syndrome, and very high levels raise the risk of sudden pancreatitis.

note.what: Total cholesterol is the overall amount of cholesterol, a waxy fat-like substance, in your blood, counting both the LDL and HDL kinds.
note.ask: Which of my lipid results are outside the healthy range for me, and how often should I be retested?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/cholesterol-levels/ (updated 15 October 2024)
note.means: A higher result usually means steps to bring cholesterol down are advised, as it adds to the risk of heart and artery disease.

note.what: HDL is the 'good' cholesterol; it helps clear LDL cholesterol out of your blood.
note.ask: Is my HDL low for my age and sex, and what changes would help raise it?
note.source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine (US) — https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/cholesterol-levels/ (updated 15 October 2024)
note.means: A lower HDL is flagged as a concern, because it gives less of that protection against heart attack and stroke.

summary:
Your blood sugar results are higher than the lab's normal range. Your average blood sugar over the past few months is also elevated. These can be signs of prediabetes or diabetes.

Your cholesterol results show concerns. Your LDL, or bad cholesterol, is high and contributes to fatty build-up in arteries. Your triglycerides are high, which adds to heart disease risk. Your HDL, or good cholesterol, is low, which means less protection for your heart and blood vessels. Your total cholesterol is also high.

Please take this report to your doctor.
